fields.description:
## Problem
A write-side transient runner-FS fault aborts store git operations routed through
`gitutil.run_git_write`, because that seam's transient-retry family covers only READ-side
signatures. The identical fault is already recognised and retried on `event_append`'s
`git add` path, so the store self-heals in one place and red-lights CI in another.

Symptom (bug `unheedful-custodial-bluebottle`): the s3 doctor's `git commit-tree` failed with
`error: unable to create temporary file: No such file or directory`, aborting
`tests/integration/test_s3_doctor.py::test_heal_folds_into_the_ref_from_a_detached_head_tracker`
with `S3DoctorConflict`. One CI shard only; the same code passed on every other shard and
locally — the fingerprint of a runner-FS blip, not a data fault.

## Root cause (confirmed on current main)
- `gitutil.run_git_write` composes `_with_index_lock_retry` (OUTER, git lock signatures)
  around `_with_transient_head_retry` (INNER).
- `_with_transient_head_retry` retries only what `_is_transient_head_error` matches:
  `_TRANSIENT_HEAD_MARKERS` (`could not parse head`) and `_TRANSIENT_OBJECT_MARKERS`
  (`bad object`). Both are READ-side faults.
- The write-side loose-object temp-create signature matches neither, so `run_git_write`
  returns it on the first attempt.
- `event_append._TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS` + `_with_transient_add_retry` DO match it, but are
  composed only into `event_append`'s `_git_add`, `_git_commit`, `_git_commit_paths` and its
  two recovery commits. Every other `run_git_write` caller — `s3_doctor`, compaction, the
  claim/transition writers — is unprotected.

## Approach
Move the write-side marker family into the shared seam and delete the private copy, so there
is exactly ONE definition and every store git caller inherits the same bounded retry. No new
heuristic dialect: the marker strings are carried over verbatim from `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS`
and the attempt/backoff shape stays the existing bounded 3-attempt, linear-backoff loop.

In `gitutil`:
- Add `_TRANSIENT_WRITE_MARKERS` (the three verbatim write-side markers) and a public
  `is_transient_object_write_error`, mirroring the existing public
  `is_transient_object_read_error` so a caller that must classify the fault in its own error
  uses the same set rather than a second private copy.
- Fold it into the transient predicate, renaming `_is_transient_head_error` ->
  `_is_transient_git_fault` and `_with_transient_head_retry` -> `_with_transient_fault_retry`
  (with `_TRANSIENT_HEAD_ATTEMPTS`/`_TRANSIENT_HEAD_BACKOFF_S` renamed to match), because the
  loop is no longer HEAD-specific. Mechanical rename; the loop body, budget and
  return-immediately-on-anything-else behaviour are unchanged.
- Give `_with_transient_fault_retry` the `attempts` keyword `_with_transient_add_retry`
  already had, so `_git_add`'s pass-through survives the merge.

In `event_append`:
- Delete `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS`, `_is_transient_add_error` and `_with_transient_add_retry`;
  re-export the shared `is_transient_object_write_error` under the existing private name so
  the current classification test keeps a symbol to assert on.
- Replace each nested `_with_transient_head_retry(lambda: _with_transient_add_retry(f))`
  composition with a single `_with_transient_fault_retry(f)`, and route `_git_add` through it
  too. This is a deliberate narrowing of an accidental budget: the nested pair currently gives
  the commit paths up to 3x3 attempts on a write fault; one loop restores the intended bounded
  3, the same budget the read-side faults get.

Idempotence precondition is already satisfied and documented: `run_git_write`'s docstring
requires it, and `add`/`commit`/`commit-tree` are content-addressed re-writes of the same
objects on the same state.

Exclusions preserved: the corrupt-object signatures the existing comments call out
(`loose object ... is corrupt`, `inflate: data stream error`) are still not matched, and a
write fault that survives the whole budget still returns its failing result, so a genuinely
persistent fault fails loudly.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` — shared write-side marker family + predicate; rename the
  now-general transient retry.
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` — delete the private copy; adopt the shared retry at its
  five composition sites and in `_git_add`.
- `tests/unit/test_gitutil_transient_write_retry.py` — new regression tests.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_event_append_transient_retry.py` — repoint the two
  classification assertions at the surviving symbol (behaviour assertions untouched).

Out of scope, not touched: `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py`,
`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`.

## Testing
New unit tests drive `run_git_write` with a fake `run_git` seam that returns a scripted
sequence of `CompletedProcess` results, counting attempts (no sleeps asserted, no timing
budgets):
- Linux ENOENT write-side stderr on attempt 1, success on attempt 2 -> `run_git_write` returns
  the success and made exactly 2 attempts.
- macOS EINVAL spelling and each sibling marker (`failed to insert into database`,
  `unable to index file`) are classified transient by `is_transient_object_write_error`.
- A corrupt-object stderr (`loose object ... is corrupt`) is NOT retried: exactly 1 attempt,
  failing result returned.
- A write-side fault on EVERY attempt returns the failing result after the bounded budget and
  does not loop forever.
- The s3 doctor inherits it: its git op driven through the seam with the fault injected once
  completes instead of raising.
Existing `test_event_append_transient_retry.py` and `test_run_git_wrapper.py` must still pass,
proving `git add` behaviour is unchanged after de-duplication.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `run_git_write` retries a write-side temp-file ENOENT/EINVAL failure — a test injects the
      failure on the first attempt and asserts the call succeeds on retry.
- [ ] The s3 doctor inherits it — a test drives a doctor git op through the seam with the fault
      injected once and asserts it completes instead of raising.
- [ ] Corrupt-object signatures are still NOT retried — a test asserts immediate surfacing.
- [ ] A write-side fault that survives the bounded budget still returns its failing result.
- [ ] The write-side marker family has exactly one definition — a grep finds no second copy,
      and `event_append`'s `git add` retry still passes its existing tests.
- [ ] The full local gate set plus CI's pytest tiers pass.
